items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: Incidentally, in this vicious band, there's a musician who became later a legitimate musician in the Sanger Theater. He became an old boss, by the name of Alessandra. He was also a peck horn player in that band... He was in the band also.

ctx.x: Well I was going to ask about the position of the bass drummer. Was he always on the left? Always on the left, as a rule. As you marched on the left, as a rule. Yeah. The bass drummer is over on your left and you were the snare drum on the right.

Unless you like, like we here, you had two and then you put the other one in the middle. And then, in those days the trombones, and if you had two trombones, well you'd have the two trombones and the bass horn. Incidentally, in this vicious band, there's a musician who became later a legitimate musician in the Sanger Theater. He became an old boss, by the name of Alessandra. He was also a peck horn player in that band and his father was a bass player. He had one of these Italian helican basses, not the Sousa for…
Did he have any saxes in the band in those days?
